body:
## Summary

A listing and a `HEAD` report **different modification times for the same object**, differing by up to 999 ms.

- `ListObjectsV2` renders `<LastModified>` via `iso8601` (`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:553`), which keeps milliseconds: `{year}-{month}-{day}T{hour}:{minute}:{second}.{millis:03}Z`. Emitted at `:956-959`.
- `GET`/`HEAD` render the `Last-Modified` header via `http_date` (`:3111`), which computes `let secs = epoch_millis / 1_000;` and discards the remainder. Emitted at `:2414-2415`.

Both read the same stored `modified` (`crates/server/src/lib.rs:197`, `:348`).

Concrete: a stored `modified = 1_700_000_000_750` lists as `2023-11-14T22:13:20.750Z` and HEADs as `Tue, 14 Nov 2023 22:13:20 GMT`.

## The header is not the defect

IMF-fixdate (RFC 7231 §7.1.1.1) has **second** granularity, so `http_date` truncating is required, not a bug. The two functions already know about each other — `iso8601`'s doc comment at `:548-549` says it is "distinct from the IMF-fixdate `http_date` uses for the `Last-Modified` *header*".

The defect is that the **listing exposes sub-second precision the header cannot represent**, so the two surfaces disagree for any object whose stamp is not exactly on a second boundary — roughly 999 in 1000.

## Why it matters

Sync and mirror tools compare modification times to decide whether to transfer. A client that lists a prefix, caches `LastModified`, then revalidates individual objects with `HEAD` sees a mismatch on **every** object, every pass — and cannot tell a real change from a formatting artefact. That is the exact failure the codebase already reasons about elsewhere: `:4468-4470` declines to fabricate a zero epoch precisely because "sync tools compare `LastModified` to decide whether to transfer".

It also blocks `sync` in the blackbox validation tool (proposal 0017, #735), whose comparison is size-and-mtime.

## To confirm before choosing a fix

**What does real S3 emit?** The belief is that AWS returns `.000Z` in listings — i.e. S3 stores second granularity, so listing and header agree by construction. That should be verified against the real service rather than assumed, because it decides the fix:

- If S3 is second-granularity: truncate `modified` to seconds at the storage boundary, or render `.000Z` in the listing. Listing and header agree, and Wyrd matches S3.
- If S3 does emit sub-second values: the divergence is S3-faithful and this issue becomes documentation plus a note for mtime-comparing clients.

Either way the current state — one surface with milliseconds and one without, undocumented — is not the answer.

## Definition of done

- A listing and a `HEAD` of the same object report times a client can reconcile.
- The chosen semantics are stated where `iso8601` and `http_date` are defined.
- A test pins listing and header agreement for a stamp that is *not* on a second boundary — the case that currently fails.

## Refs

`crates/gateway-s3/src/lib.rs:548-570` (`iso8601`), `:3104-3136` (`http_date`), `:956-959`, `:2414-2415` · `crates/server/src/lib.rs:197,348,756` · ADR-0047 · Found while reviewing proposal 0017 (#735).

title: s3: listing and HEAD report different Last-Modified for the same object (ms vs second granularity)
